atoms.claim: The five-node direct Q multiplexer selects each arbitrary Q-valued payload exactly.
Five operation nodes are necessary in the declared local d/u DAG grammar with dynamic value names available as terminals.
The code 0->10, 1->01, 2->00 uses two one-node rails and a one-node decoder.
The complete direct-Q/signed-outer DAG computes every checked compatible selector.
For every r>=64 the declared compiler has size below 8*3^r/r.
For every r>=64 the declared compiler has depth at most r+6ceil(log2 r)+9.
The new scoped Lean mux/code source has been compiled with the pinned toolchain.
The size-depth Pareto points are globally optimal among all d/u DAGs.
The direct-Q Pareto construction is publication-novel and clear of relevant prior art.
